title: An Integrated DFT-Wannier-Quantum Embedding Pipeline for Strongly Correlated Materials: Scaling Benchmarks in Li-hBN
abstract: The seamless integration of Density Functional Theory (DFT) with quantum variational algorithms is essential for the predictive simulation of strongly correlated materials. In this work, we present an end-to-end computational pipeline - comprising DFT geometry relaxation, non-self-consistent field (NSCF) calculations, and Wannier-based orbital localization - to prepare active-space Hamiltonians for quantum embedding. We utilize the Adaptive Variational Quantum Eigensolver (ADAPT-VQE) framework, significantly enhanced by a Greedy-Operator Commutativity Partitioning (GOCP) approach and a Taylor-expanded O(5) operator evolution strategy to efficiently manage the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space. We demonstrate this framework through a systematic benchmark study of Li-hBN, mapping the system onto qubit registers and investigating the convergence behavior as the active space is expanded from 8 to 14 spatial orbitals. Our results quantify the relationship between active-space size and computational demand, identifying a critical "scaling wall" where classical simulation costs transition from manageable to intractable. This study provides a rigorous performance baseline for the DFT-to-ADAPT-VQE workflow and offers empirical insights into the memory and processing limits currently facing hybrid quantum-classical architectures using advanced co-processing strategies.
summary: The paper introduces an integrated computational pipeline combining DFT with ADAPT-VQE to simulate strongly correlated materials like Li-hBN. By using Wannier functions and advanced tensor network techniques (MPS), it overcomes the exponential memory wall associated with large active spaces. This establishes a rigorous performance baseline for future hybrid quantum-classical simulations in condensed matter physics.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a scalable computational method to accurately simulate strongly correlated electronic systems, which are difficult for standard DFT methods.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated an end-to-end pipeline that can process up to 28 active orbitals by employing tensor network techniques, establishing a clear performance benchmark for hybrid quantum-classical simulation.
method: The approach integrates DFT calculations with the ADAPT-VQE framework, enhanced by GOCP and MPS tensor networks to manage the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space.
model_or_system: The study uses Lithium Hexagonal Boron Nitride (Li-hBN) as a benchmark system. The electronic structure is modeled via Wannier functions derived from DFT, leading to an active-space Hamiltonian suitable for quantum embedding.
key_observables: Variational energies calculated by ADAPT-VQE; the relationship between active-space size and computational demand.
important_parameters: Active space size (benchmarked from 8 to 14 spatial orbitals); MPS bond dimension ($\chi_{\max} = 64$); singular value truncation threshold ($\epsilon_{	ext{trunc}} = 10^{-8}$).
main_assumptions: The primary limitation addressed is the exponential scaling of the Hilbert space, necessitating the use of bounded tensor networks (MPS) for tractability.

why_interesting: This work provides a crucial blueprint for applying quantum computing methods (like VQE) to condensed matter problems, specifically addressing the resource scaling issues inherent in simulating strongly correlated materials beyond current hardware limits.
